t: You're looking at a building on Grosvenor Gardens in Westminster, numbered 36 to 50. It was designed by Thomas Cundy the Third, a British architect who followed his grandfather and father into the family practice in the 1840s. He also served as surveyor of the Grosvenor Estate, which is why his work appears around this part of London. He retired from that post in 1890, and Eustace Balfour took over from him.
